proposed_definition_changes.reason: The current rule always chooses the first free column. A zero coefficient matrix with a two-coordinate contrast supported only on its second coordinate is a counterexample: the first fundamental vector has zero query contrast, while the second is separating. Scanning the fundamental null vectors for the first nonzero contrast preserves canonicity and is exactly what inconsistency of the augmented row-space system guarantees.

open_obligations.what_is_open: A finite global theorem connecting exhaustive context-compatible factor failure to jointly quotient-supported, multi-block rooted-forest perturbations with zero full observed increment and nonzero full-query increment, together with total arithmetic recovery in every remaining case.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen primitives provide neither a complete normal form for cross-context recovery nor a gluing theorem. A local C-forest does not imply a global direction after quotient row sharing, as the reference-context bow proves; conversely, exhausting an active deletion can erase the only usable forest, as the five-node example proves. Generic real-algebraic feasibility would decide semantic fibers but would not establish the required forest-linked dichotomy or descent to the permitted arithmetic-expression class.
open_obligations.attempted: The proof was reduced first to retained partial traces and then to row-space tests on residual forest-supported blocks. The one-block fixed-nuisance sink case closes exactly. Extending it by blockwise nullspace intersection fails without controlling changes in nuisance tables and cross-district cancellation; local separating directions can be killed by shared rows, and separate surviving directions need not combine to change the full query.
